options: Colicky right-upper-quadrant pain radiating to shoulder/back

history.ask: Drugs, herbs & alcohol in the last 3 months

options: Contact with a jaundiced person, unsafe water or food
Transfusion, surgery, dental work, tattooing, or injections
Marked weight loss with poor appetite

history.ask: Personal or family history of anemia, gallstones, or splenectomy
Episodes triggered by fasting, stress, or minor illness
Confusion, day–night sleep reversal, easy bruising, or abdominal swelling

red_flags: Fever with rigors + right-upper-quadrant pain + jaundice (Charcot triad — ascending cholangitis)
Confusion, drowsiness, or flapping tremor — hepatic encephalopathy / fulminant failure
Bleeding tendency: hematemesis, melena, or easy bruising
Painless progressive jaundice with weight loss after age 50
exam: Grade the depth of scleral and skin icterus
Palpate the liver: size, tenderness, edge and surface character
Feel for a palpable non-tender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign)
Search for stigmata of chronic liver disease: spider nevi, palmar erythema, gynecomastia
Test for asterixis and assess orientation
Check conjunctivae for pallor and skin for scratch marks
Palpate cervical and left supraclavicular lymph nodes

investigations.why: The branch point: isolated indirect bilirubin = hemolysis or Gilbert; ALT/AST in the hundreds = viral/drug/alcoholic hepatitis; ALP-predominant rise = biliary obstruction
Anemia with reticulocytosis rules hemolysis in; a completely normal CBC with isolated indirect bilirubin supports Gilbert syndrome

investigations.test: Viral serology: HBsAg, anti-HCV, anti-HAV IgM
investigations.why: Rules acute viral hepatitis in or out — the commonest medical jaundice in this setting
Dilated bile ducts separate surgical (stone / pancreatic-head mass) from medical jaundice; also shows gallstones, liver texture, splenomegaly, and ascites
Measures synthetic failure — the severity marker in hepatitis and cirrhosis, and the screen behind the bleeding red flag
Bilirubinuria present in obstructive and hepatocellular jaundice but absent in hemolysis — a cheap bedside discriminator
Detects renal impairment complicating sepsis with cholangitis or advanced cirrhosis — changes urgency
Second-line — if ultrasound shows dilated ducts or a mass: defines the level and cause of obstruction (ductal stone vs pancreatic-head carcinoma)

supports: Flu-like prodrome then jaundice over days
Contact with jaundice, unsafe water, or blood exposure
Tender enlarged liver with dark urine
History of gallstones or positive Murphy's sign
